displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest realist case treats objective moral reasons as the best account of rational criticism across changing desires, with defeasible appearances providing initial but revisable access to elementary evaluative truths.

novelty.explanation: Integrates the realist metaphysical and epistemological routes while making their conclusions explicitly defeasible and proportionate.

premises.text: Agents can rationally criticize present, future, higher-order, and identity-defining desires, so the mere location or strength of a desire cannot exhaust normative authority.

novelty.explanation: Develops the transcript's counterexamples into a general constraint on desire-based authority.

premises.text: The most economical common explanation of such criticism is that some considerations count in favor of action independently of whichever desire presently dominates.

novelty.explanation: Adds the positive bridge from desire insufficiency to attitude-independent reasons.

premises.text: Appearances can supply initial justification without guaranteeing truth, provided their force is reduced by disagreement, causal debunking, incoherence, and contrary evidence.

novelty.explanation: Specifies defeater controls answering the concern about indiscriminate credulity.

premises.text: Elementary judgments about gratuitous suffering remain comparatively stable under informed reflection and therefore deserve evidential weight unless a stronger defeating explanation is supplied.

novelty.explanation: Turns initial plausibility into a modest reflective-stability claim rather than a conclusive proof.

premises.text: Judgment-led changes in motivation are compatible with emotions and desires also influencing judgment, so realism needs reciprocal causation rather than cognition-only motivation.

novelty.explanation: Narrows the motivational claim to resist the projectivist reply.

conclusion.text: Objective moral reasons are a credible explanation of rational criticism, and carefully defeasible appearances can justify limited elementary moral beliefs, although neither claim excludes revision or further naturalistic explanation.

novelty.explanation: States a proportionate realist conclusion that preserves both metaphysical and epistemic uncertainty.

newArguments.title: Cross-standpoint correction
newArguments.text: A desire theory can explain why an agent endorses a commitment, but rational criticism often persists when every currently endorsed preference favors the mistake. Cases involving manipulated identities, adaptive preferences, or coherent cruelty suggest that stability and self-centrality are not sufficient for authority. Objective reasons offer a unified explanation: standpoint features affect access and motivation, while the consideration's normative force need not be created by endorsement. This does not prove realism, but it identifies explanatory work that a purely internal account must reproduce without covert evaluation.

novelty.explanation: Introduces manipulated and adaptive standpoints as a new test for accounts of normative authority.

newArguments.title: Defeater-sensitive convergence
newArguments.text: Appearance-based justification becomes more discriminating when paired with explicit defeaters. An elementary moral appearance gains credibility when it survives factual correction, imaginative variation, awareness of framing, and scrutiny from differently situated agents; it loses credibility when those checks reveal distortion. This model neither treats seeming as certainty nor requires best-explanation reasoning to create all initial justification. It instead assigns explanatory reasoning a crucial revising role, thereby preserving the foundational insight while answering the concern that appearances indiscriminately validate whatever anyone happens to feel.

novelty.explanation: Adds operational checks that repair the underdeveloped account of defeaters.

thesis.text: The strongest error-theoretic case explains normative practice through structured agent-relative reasons and treats moral appearances as psychologically informative but insufficient evidence for attitude-independent moral facts.

novelty.explanation: Integrates the con routes while avoiding a categorical inference from social origin alone.

premises.text: Practical reasons can be indexed to an agent's informed and coherent concerns without making momentary motivational strength the measure of normative weight.

novelty.explanation: Strengthens desire dependence by separating reasons from overpowering impulses.

premises.text: Self-conception has authority only when it survives information, consistency, diachronic stability, and scrutiny of manipulation, rather than merely occupying a higher psychological level.

novelty.explanation: Answers the arbitrary higher-order desire objection with explicit constraints.

premises.text: Moral experience can result from projection, social learning, emotional salience, and concept acquisition even if moral belief later reciprocally influences motivation.

novelty.explanation: Preserves projectivism without requiring an implausibly exclusive causal direction.

premises.text: Evidence for a distinctive domain of facts should increase when those facts contribute explanatory or predictive success beyond the psychological and social mechanisms already available.

novelty.explanation: Recasts explanationism as a comparative evidential demand rather than a universal necessary condition.

premises.text: Intellectual confidence and conceptual competence can explain some nonperceptual justification without establishing that every forceful seeming directly represents an independent fact.

novelty.explanation: Develops the empiricist account while limiting its scope.

conclusion.text: Moral error theory remains credible if structured standpoint-relative reasons explain practical criticism and naturalistic mechanisms explain moral appearances without additional predictive contribution from objective moral facts.

novelty.explanation: Makes the conclusion conditional upon explanatory success rather than treating social embeddedness as decisive.

newArguments.title: Counterfactual explanatory contribution
newArguments.text: Instead of requiring every justified belief to arise from best explanation, the skeptic can ask a narrower question: what observable or inferential difference would objective moral facts make after psychological dispositions, social learning, factual beliefs, and deliberative consistency are held fixed? If rival realist theories predict conflicting obligations while sharing the same ordinary evidence, their additional facts may have limited discriminating power. This argument does not show that explanatory idleness entails falsity; it supplies a defeater against claiming knowledge until some distinctive contribution is identified.

novelty.explanation: Introduces a counterfactual intervention test for the evidential contribution of objective moral facts.

newArguments.title: Procedural authority without categorical reasons
newArguments.text: The self-conception proposal can be strengthened procedurally. A commitment gains practical authority when it is informed, coherent with enduring concerns, resistant to manipulation, and endorsed across temporally separated deliberative perspectives. These conditions remain grounded in the agent while excluding spontaneous higher-order urges and many adaptive distortions. The account still permits external criticism by showing that a person has false factual beliefs, procedural inconsistency, or commitments that frustrate other stable concerns. Its remaining burden is to explain apparently rational criticism of a fully informed and coherent but morally abhorrent standpoint.

novelty.explanation: Supplies a nonarbitrary procedural hierarchy and openly preserves its hardest residual case.
